beats.say: Velcro is called a perfect copy of a burr. Its inventor's own patent says the first try barely worked.
George de Mestral said the idea came in nineteen forty-one, from burrs stuck in his dog's ears.
In nineteen fifty-one he patented nylon hooks on both strips, hooks grabbing hooks. But his later patent admits only about thirty percent ever caught.
So in nineteen fifty-seven he gave one side soft loops. About a thousand in every square centimetre, and far more hooks catch.
And a 2015 study says Velcro works less like a burr than like a different plant. The perfect copy was never that simple.
